### 1. What the caller expresses, and what the simulator does

The caller (Marguerite Thornbury, Pinehurst Analytics Group) states the object, the timing, the boundary and the mode of authorisation clearly:
- object — "the August micro market bill", the market "on the fourth floor at the Chicago office"; account code `CA-44207`, billing postcode `60614`, direct line `5035118427`, PO `PO-PN-2026-118`;
- timing — "she wants to settle the August invoice today";
- boundary/authorisation — "she would rather run the payment herself from her own banking screen than have the desk move money on her behalf … the money leaves on her instruction, by bank transfer out of their own payables run"; and "She is happy for the desk to put the account straight first and says so plainly".

The simulator only conveys needs and answers conditionally: "She cannot say what the invoice comes to … would rather be told what the desk makes it"; "If the agent tells her something else has to be put right on the account before the bill can be settled, she says that is fine and to carry on; she has no view on what it is". She executes one user-owned tool at the agent's direction: "Once the agent has unlocked the payment for her and told her the amount and the invoice it goes against, she runs it herself on the spot, by bank transfer, and reads back the confirmation". She never states a figure and never pushes the procedure along. No policy or GT leaks through her.

### 4. Each scored parameter, in words, with inputs, tiers and value

Printed figures read for **Standard Micro Market**: equipment lease 480 USD/month and installation lead 25 days (*Micro Market Format Entry Thresholds and Installation Charges*); 280 distinct products, 45 fresh and chilled, frozen unit **included** (*Fixture, Range and Kiosk Specification by Market Format*); 3 restocking visits each week, call-out charge 145 USD (*Restocking Rounds, Planogram Changes and Call-Out Charges*); subsidy true-up basis, card processing 2.6 per cent, invoice raised on day 10 (*Settlement Basis, Shelf Pricing and Portfolio Bands*); payment terms 30 calendar days (*Payment Terms, Late Charges and Credit Hold Thresholds*); share of shelf price 20 per cent, daily ceiling 5.50 USD, smallest funding lot 4200 USD, lot drawable 12 months (*Client Subsidy Terms Printed against Each Micro Market Format*); availability guarantee 97.5 per cent, credit 1 per cent of settlement per outage hour, ceiling on credits in one period 20 per cent, claim window 21 days (*Kiosk Availability Guarantees and Service Credit Rates by Micro Market Format*).

- approved `planogram_change_request`: 2 in the 3 months (2026-08-24, 2026-07-13) and 2 in the 12 months;
- approved `resumption_request`: 2 in the 12 months (2026-07-09, 2026-02-18); approved `suspension_request`: 1 in the 3 months (2026-07-02), 2 in the 12 months;
- `shrink_dispute`: one `in_review` (2026-09-07, IC-24118) and one `approved` (2026-06-20, IC-23907), both inside 6 months; most recent shrink adjustment 312.40 USD posted 2026-09-05;
- `settlement_payment` rows: 3 in the 12 months (2026-06-12, 2026-07-12, 2026-08-28), the last of them 882.15 USD and inside the 2 months;
- `market_monthly_settlement_invoiced` rows in the 2 months (from 2026-07-22): equipment_fee 480.00 and monthly_settlement 402.15 on 2026-08-10, equipment_fee 480.00 on 2026-09-10;

- installation completed 2025-02-10 → market open ~19 months.

**(a) The late-booked client discount** — *Settlement Bureau Basis: the Client Discount Booked for a Kiosk Trip Rung Without It*: "the trip is valued from the agreement's own drawdown record, that value is grossed back to a shelf figure at the share of shelf price printed against the market format, the share that applies to the trip is applied to that shelf figure, and the discount so obtained is held to the daily ceiling printed against the market format."
- *Valuing a Kiosk Trip for a Late-Booked Client Discount*: 11 drawdowns ≥ 8 in the quarter **and** an approved kiosk outage request in the same quarter → tier 1, "the trip is valued at the mean drawdown taken over the reading window".
- *How Far Back the Mean Kiosk Drawdown is Read*: 11 drawdowns < 12 in the quarter **and** market open 19 months ≥ 12 → "the twelve months to that day". Mean = 47.15 / 18 = 2.619444 → **2.62 USD**.
- Shelf figure = 2.62 / 20 per cent = **13.10 USD** (the gross-back is expressly at the market format's printed share).
- *Which Printed Share Governs a Kiosk Trip where the Client also Holds a Site Cafe*: active cafe contract **and** 21500 USD ≥ 18000 USD of cafe subsidy over the trailing year → "the share of menu price printed against the cafe service model governs both outlets together" = **25 per cent** (Full Service Cafe, from the cafe programme's own subsidy schedule).
- *How Deeply a Client has Funded its Micro Market*: funding lots in the trailing 12 months = 1 (only the 2026-08-14 lot of 4200; the 2025-09-05 lot falls outside) → "1 lot or none meets it" → thin-funding step of **4 percentage points taken off the share**. Share applied = 25 − 4 = **21 per cent**.
- 13.10 × 21 per cent = 2.751 → **2.75 USD**; the daily ceiling of 5.50 USD does not bind.
- **Parameter: `subsidy_amount_usd` = 2.75**, `service_period` = `2026-09`, `source_reference` = `POS-40516903`, `market_agreement_id` = `1543ba77-…`.

**(b) The product settlement for 2026-08** — *Working the Product Settlement of a Micro Market that Settles on a Subsidy True-Up*: "the client discount met at the kiosk over the reading window, taken at the true-up share, together with the card processing charge on the shelf value of those trips, the call-out charge for unscheduled planogram work, and the fresh handling charge."
- *The Window over which Kiosk Discount is Read*: 11 (now 12) drawdowns ≥ 10 **and** an approved kiosk outage request in the same quarter → "taken over the six months to that day and halved". Discount met over 6 months = 38.80 + the 2.75 just booked = 41.55; halved = 20.775 → **20.78 USD**.
- *Prompt and Carrying True-Up Shares*: 3 settlement payments ≥ 3 in the 12 months **and** balance unsettled 1016.15 < 4200 → **97 per cent**. True-up = 20.78 × 97 per cent = **20.16 USD**.
- Shelf value = 20.78 / 20 per cent = 103.90 USD. *Fresh Trade and the Card Processing Rate Passed Through*: format carries a frozen unit **and** fresh-cabinet share of the quarter's trips 4/12 = 33.3 per cent ≥ 33 per cent → 2.6 + 0.25 = **2.85 per cent**. Card charge = 103.90 × 2.85 per cent = 2.9612 → **2.96 USD**.
- *Approved Planogram Changes and the Call-Out Charge*: 2 approved changes ≥ 2 in the quarter **and** 280 distinct products ≥ 250 → twice 145.00 = **290.00 USD**.
- *The Fresh Handling Charge Raised where the Fresh Cabinet has been Shopped*: 6 fresh-cabinet trips ≥ 6 over the half year **and** the coolers shopped (4 chilled trips) → 145.00 × 6/(6+4) = **87.00 USD**.
- **Parameter: `settlement_amount_usd` = 20.16 + 2.96 + 290.00 + 87.00 = 400.12**, `invoice_reference` = `INV-MK-440318`, `service_period` = `2026-08`.

**(c) The outage credit against INV-MK-440318** — *Calculating the Credit Allowed for Hours a Micro Market Kiosk Could Not Take a Payment*: "the chargeable hours at the credit rate, applied to the settlement charged on the agreement over the two months to the day the credit is worked out, together with the empty-market step on that same settlement, the two figures being added before the allowed share is taken of them, and the whole held to the ceiling on credits in one settlement period".
- *Availability Guarantees and the Span over which Approved Kiosk Outage is Read*: guarantee 97.5 per cent ≥ 97.5 **and** 8 approved outage requests ≥ 5 in the quarter → "the hours are read over the six months to that day" → **11 hours**.
- *Charging Kiosk Outage Hours as Booked where the Outage is Material*: 11 ≥ 8 **and** 2 declined requests over the half year → "as booked less one hour for each declined request" → chargeable hours = **9**.
- *The Age of a Micro Market and the Weight on Its Credit Rate*: open 19 months < 24 **and** 8 ≥ 3 approved outage requests in the quarter → 1 per cent × 1.5 = **1.5 per cent**.
- Settlement over the two months = 480.00 + 402.15 + 480.00 + 400.12 (the charge just raised) = **1762.27 USD** (see the openness recorded under "counter-proof" below).
- Figure = 9 × 1.5 per cent × 1762.27 = **237.91 USD**. *The Empty-Market Step Credited where a Micro Market has been Reopened Repeatedly*: 2 approved resumptions ≥ 2 in the year **and** restocked 3 times each week ≥ 3 → 2 per cent of the settlement = **35.25 USD**.
- *Time the Client Had the Market Closed Off, and the Share of an Outage Credit Allowed*: an approved suspension request in the quarter **and** 11 ≥ 8 approved outage requests over the half year → **75 per cent**. (237.91 + 35.25) × 75 per cent = **204.87 USD**. Ceiling = 20 per cent × 1762.27 = 352.45 USD, which does not bind.
- **Parameter: `credit_amount_usd` = 204.87**, `invoice_reference` = `INV-MK-440318`, `service_period` = `2026-08`.

**(d) The amount tendered** — *Working Out the Amount a Client Tenders on a Micro Market Settlement Invoice*: "the settlement charges read over that window, plus the shrink adjustments posted over the two months … less the credits set against the settlement and less the settlement payments already recorded over those same two months … never taken below nothing", then the withheld amount, then the prompt-settlement discount, then the group-settlement offset, "one after the other on a shrinking figure".
- *Several Charges on the Agreement, and the Span over which They are Read for a Tender*: 2 or more settlement charges in the two months **and** the format invoiced on day 10 ("on or after the tenth day") → "the charges are read over those two months" = **1762.27 USD**.
- Shrink over the two months = **312.40 USD** (2026-09-05; the 2026-06-14 adjustment is outside).
- *Several Credits Standing … and How Much is Set Against the Settlement*: 2 credits (45.00 of 2026-09-02 and the 204.87 just allowed) ≥ 2 over the two months **and** balance unsettled below the printed minimum funding lot of 4200 → **60 per cent** → 249.87 × 60 per cent = **149.92 USD**.
- Settlement payments over the two months = **882.15 USD** (2026-08-28).
- Balance standing = 1762.27 + 312.40 − 149.92 − 882.15 = **1042.60 USD**.
- *Shrink Disputes Standing in Review and the Amount Withheld*: one dispute `in_review` **and** one `approved` over the half year → "the whole of the most recent shrink adjustment posted on the agreement" = **312.40 USD** withheld → 730.20 USD.
- *Settling a Micro Market Invoice Well Before It Falls Due*: the invoice was raised 2026-09-10 (read "from the equipment line the settlement invoice carries"), terms 30 days, so 18 days to run ≥ 15, **and** 3 ≥ 3 settlement payments over the year → deep prompt discount **1.5 per cent** = 10.95 → 719.25 USD.
- *The Group Offset Given where a Client also Settles a Workplace Cafe Contract*: the cafe contract carries nothing unsettled (`receivable_balance_usd 0.0`) **and** 3 ≥ 2 cafe invoice payments over the quarter → **2 per cent** = 14.38 → **704.87 USD**.
- **Parameters: `payment_amount_usd` = 704.87**, `payment_channel` = `ach` ("where the client sends it by bank transfer out of their own accounts payable run"), `invoice_reference` = `INV-MK-440318`, `service_period` = `2026-08`.

1. `find_customers(client_account_code="CA-44207")` → agent.
2. `verify_caller_identity(customer_id, client_account_code="CA-44207", billing_zip_code="60614")` → agent. Forward dependency: nothing may be quoted or moved before it passes.
3. `find_market_agreements`, `find_market_ledger`, `find_market_service_intake`, `find_cafe_contracts`, `find_cafe_ledger` → agent (reads).
4. `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool` + `call_agent_discoverable_tool` `post_kiosk_catch_up_drawdown_96ce656f` (agent-owned) with `{market_agreement_id, service_period:"2026-09", source_reference:"POS-40516903", subsidy_amount_usd:2.75}`.
5. `post_market_settlement_true_up_13e3670a` (agent-owned) with `{market_agreement_id, invoice_reference:"INV-MK-440318", service_period:"2026-08", settlement_amount_usd:400.12}` — backward dependency on 4 (the settlement reads the drawdown record).
6. `issue_market_outage_credit_49294a76` (agent-owned) with `{market_agreement_id, invoice_reference:"INV-MK-440318", service_period:"2026-08", credit_amount_usd:204.87}` — backward dependency on 5 (the credit is measured on the settlement charged).
7. `unlock_user_discoverable_tool("pay_market_settlement_invoice_693f0fba")`, then the **customer** calls `call_user_discoverable_tool` with `{market_agreement_id, invoice_reference:"INV-MK-440318", service_period:"2026-08", payment_channel:"ach", payment_amount_usd:704.87}` — backward dependency on 5 and 6.

Terminal state: `INV-MK-440318` carries the equipment line, the 400.12 product settlement, the 204.87 outage credit and a settlement payment of 704.87 recorded by the client; the agreement's drawdown record carries the 2.75 catch-up drawdown; the caller is told the amount and the invoice and rings off.

### 6. The problem tree derived from the visible materials alone

**Problems, direction, order.**

```
post_kiosk_catch_up_drawdown  ──▶  post_market_settlement_true_up  ──▶  issue_market_outage_credit  ──▶  pay_market_settlement_invoice
                                                      └──────────────────────────────────────────────────▶  (also blocks the payment directly)
```
Handling order: catch-up drawdown → product settlement → outage credit → client's payment. The customer mentioned only the last of the four.

**Hop 1 — the payment waits on the product settlement.** *Recording a Client's Settlement of a Micro Market Invoice* states, on the blocked side: "The amount tendered against a settlement invoice is not settled before the product settlement for that period stands charged on the agreement. While that period's product settlement does not yet stand charged on the agreement, the amount tendered is not settled." Query: `find_market_ledger` shows `INV-MK-440318` carrying only `equipment_fee 480.0` (2026-09-10) and `shrink_adjustment 312.4` (2026-09-05) — no `monthly_settlement` row for period `2026-08`, while every earlier invoice (`INV-MK-438720`, `-439311`, `-439902`) carries one. So the waited-on state does not hold. Searching on the words the sentence and the records use — "product settlement", "monthly settlement charge", "settlement invoice" — reaches *Invoicing a Micro Market's Product Settlement for a Settlement Period*, whose own rule describes the write: "one call adding a single monthly settlement charge to the named settlement invoice on that agreement's ledger". **state-derived.**

**Hop 2 — the payment waits on a credit naming the kiosk.** Same document: "The amount tendered against a settlement invoice is not settled before a service credit carrying the kiosk whose lost hours it answers stands allowed against that invoice. While no such credit, carrying the kiosk whose lost hours it answers, stands allowed against that invoice, the amount tendered is not settled." Query: the only `market_service_credit_issued` row is 45.00 USD against `INV-MK-439902` with `kiosk_reference: ''` — it names no kiosk and is against another invoice. The words "credit … carrying the kiosk whose lost hours it answers" lead to *Allowing a Client Credit for Kiosk Outage against a Micro Market Settlement Invoice*: "The credit is set against the named invoice, carries the settlement period it relates to, and **names the kiosk whose lost hours it answers**" — and away from *Handing Back Lapsed Subsidy Funding*, which says of its own credit that it "carries no kiosk at all". **state-derived.**

**Hop 3 — the outage credit waits on the product settlement.** *Allowing a Client Credit …*: "The credit allowed for a settlement period is fixed only after the product settlement for that period stands charged on the agreement. Until that period's product settlement stands charged on the agreement, the credit for it is not yet fixed." Confirmed unmet by the same ledger return. This also has a visible arithmetic reason: the credit is "applied to the settlement charged on the agreement over the two months to the day the credit is worked out", and that window would otherwise be missing the August charge. **state-derived.**

**Hop 4 — the product settlement waits on the drawdown record.** *Invoicing a Micro Market's Product Settlement …*: "The settlement invoiced for a period is not worked out before the agreement's drawdown record carries the client discount owed for every kiosk trip the till failed to meet. While the agreement's drawdown record is short of the discount owed for any such trip, the settlement for that period is not yet worked out." Query: `find_market_service_intake` shows a `service_credit_claim` with `request_status 'received'`, `created_at 2026-09-14`, `related_reference 'POS-40516903'`; `find_market_ledger` shows drawdowns for POS-40516742, -40516188, -40517201, -40517655, -40518104 … but **no drawdown row carrying POS-40516903**. So a kiosk trip on the agreement has no discount met against it. The words "client discount owed for a kiosk trip the till failed to meet" lead to *Late-Booked Client Discounts on Micro Market Kiosk Trips*: "A kiosk shopping trip … is sometimes rung without the client discount the till should have met. The discount is then booked to the agreement afterwards as a drawdown against the client's funding", whose `source_reference` parameter is "the kiosk till transaction that caused the drawdown … POS- followed by 8 digits". **state-derived.**

No hop was **pre-solved**: no document names another problem's tool, no document states an order between problems beyond the four prerequisite sentences above, and each tool name appears only inside its own hub's invocation block (verified by a scan of the 67 documents for the seven `*_<8 hex>` tool tokens: each occurs in exactly one document).

### Two-way counter-proof

**The conclusion is fully supported.** Every number above rests on a printed schedule figure or a tool-query return, quoted in §4.

**Closest alternatives, and what excludes them.**
- *Pay against a different invoice.* Excluded by the caller ("the August micro market bill") together with the ledger: `INV-MK-440318` is the only invoice with `service_period '2026-08'` and the only one with no `settlement_payment` row.
- *Move the money for her.* Excluded by *Recording a Client's Settlement …*: "It is the customer's own tool: the desk unlocks it and hands it over, and the customer themselves runs it", which matches her stated boundary.
- *Tender the face of the invoice (480.00 + 312.40).* Excluded by the same document's computation face: "What a client … tenders is the balance standing on the agreement over the charge-reading window **rather than the face of one invoice alone**".
- *Take the prompt discount and the group offset together.* Excluded by "so that the two reductions act one after the other on a shrinking figure rather than being added together and taken once".
- *Value the trip at the most recent drawdown.* Excluded by *Valuing a Kiosk Trip for a Late-Booked Client Discount* tier 1 on the counted records (11 drawdowns, an approved outage request in the quarter).
- *Use the market's own 20 per cent share for the trip.* Excluded by *Which Printed Share Governs a Kiosk Trip where the Client also Holds a Site Cafe* on `find_cafe_contracts` (`status 'active'`) and `find_cafe_ledger` (21500 USD over the year).
- *Widen the mean over every drawdown ever posted.* Excluded by the second line of *How Far Back the Mean Kiosk Drawdown is Read* — the market has been open 19 months, not fewer than 12.

**A boundary the visible corpus leaves open (recorded as a policy-side note, not as a document defect).** Three computation faces read "the settlement charges" / "the settlement charged on the agreement" over a window (*Working Out the Amount a Client Tenders*, *Calculating the Credit Allowed for Hours …*, *Several Charges on the Agreement …*), and no document says which ledger postings those words pick out. The records offer two readings: (i) every `market_monthly_settlement_invoiced` posting, i.e. `equipment_fee` **and** `monthly_settlement` (and, on the sibling task, `restocking_fee`); or (ii) only the `monthly_settlement` charge the two settlement tools post, which is what *Invoicing a Micro Market's Product Settlement …* calls "a single monthly settlement charge … where it joins the equipment line". I take reading (i) — the event the records themselves name "monthly settlement invoiced" — and note that reading (ii) yields, on this world, an outage credit of 93.27 USD and a tender of **0.00 USD**, at which the prompt-settlement discount and the group-settlement offset can no longer move the figure at all. The degeneracy of (ii) is my ground for preferring (i), not a sentence in the corpus.

**The wrong answer "do only the one thing the customer asked for" is excluded.** Calling `pay_market_settlement_invoice` alone leaves the governed result in a state the visible principles do not allow: "While that period's product settlement does not yet stand charged on the agreement, the amount tendered is not settled", and "While no such credit, carrying the kiosk whose lost hours it answers, stands allowed against that invoice, the amount tendered is not settled". Both states are visibly false in the ledger. The exclusion is carried by the blocked policy's own prerequisite sentences — the source's own form — and by no tool name, route or chain.

**The fall-back number (no factor applied) is computable, definite and different.** Reading only *Settlement Bureau Basis* + *Working the Product Settlement* + *Calculating the Credit* + *Working Out the Amount a Client Tenders* with the product figures they name: the trip is valued at the most recent drawdown 3.05 USD → shelf 15.25 → 20 per cent → 3.05 USD booked; the discount met over the 3-month reading window is 26.60 + 3.05 = 29.65, true-up at 100 per cent = 29.65, shelf value 148.25, card at 2.6 per cent = 3.85, nothing for planogram work or fresh handling → product settlement **33.50 USD**; hours read over 3 months = 8, halved and rounded down = 4 chargeable hours, at 1 per cent of (480 + 402.15 + 480 + 33.50) = 1395.65, no empty-market step, allowed share 100 per cent → credit **55.83 USD**; charges read over the month to the day = 480 + 33.50 = 513.50, plus shrink 312.40, less credits at 100 per cent (45.00 + 55.83) and less payments 882.15 → below nothing → **0.00 USD** tendered. Definite, and different from 704.87.

**How each factor document was reached from the customer's records** (the words the records use, not the computation document's wording):
- *Valuing a Kiosk Trip …*, *The Window over which Kiosk Discount is Read*, *How Far Back the Mean Kiosk Drawdown is Read* — from the `market_subsidy_drawdown_posted` rows and their `posted_date`s, and from `installation_completed_date 2025-02-10`.
- *How Deeply a Client has Funded its Micro Market* — from the `market_subsidy_funding_posted` rows and `subsidy_pool_balance_usd`.
- *Which Printed Share Governs a Kiosk Trip …* and *The Group Offset Given where a Client also Settles a Workplace Cafe Contract* — from `find_cafe_contracts` (`Full Service Cafe`, `status 'active'`, `receivable_balance_usd 0.0`) and `find_cafe_ledger` (`cafe_subsidy_drawdown_posted`, `cafe_invoice_payment_posted`); both documents name the Workplace Cafe Management Program by its official name and say which cafe entries they read.
- *Prompt and Carrying True-Up Shares*, *Settling a Micro Market Invoice Well Before It Falls Due*, *Several Credits Standing …* — from the `market_settlement_payment_posted` rows and `receivable_balance_usd 1016.15`.

### The 1-cent divergence, traced

Root cause is a single half-cent tie. The six-month discount met is 38.80 + 2.75 = 41.55; halved it is exactly 20.775.

- The published rounding rule in every computation document is "a figure falling exactly on the half-cent going to the nearest even cent". Nearest even cent of 20.775 is **20.78**, which gives a true-up of 20.16, a shelf value of 103.90, a card charge of 2.96 and a settlement of **400.12** — my blind figure.
- The source's own arithmetic binds `window_subsidy = RND(drawdowns_6m / 2, 2)` where `RND` is `round(float(x), 2)`; in binary floating point 41.55/2 is 20.774999…, so it returns **20.77**, giving a true-up of 20.15, a shelf value of 103.85, a card charge of 2.96 and **400.11**.
- On the strict literal reading of the computation document — "**The four amounts** are each rounded to the nearest cent … as they are taken and are then added" — the halved figure is not one of the four and is never rounded: 20.775 × 97 per cent = 20.15175 → 20.15, and 20.775 / 20 per cent = 103.875 at 2.85 per cent = 2.9604 → 2.96, giving **400.11**, the gold value.

So the corpus does entail the gold value, on the reading that rounds only the four amounts. I took the other reading, generalising from the five sibling computation documents, which all say "Each figure is rounded to the nearest cent … as it is taken" or "Every intermediate figure and the result are rounded". The divergence propagates one cent into the tender (704.87 against 704.86) and nowhere else: the outage credit is unaffected because 1762.27 and 1762.26 round the same way at every step.

This is recorded as a **policy-side defect surfaced by the documents**, not as a mistranslation: the documents carry the source's rule text verbatim, and the contradiction is between the tie-break the source publishes (nearest even cent) and the tie-break the source's own compute performs (Python float `round`, which resolves this tie downward). See `policy_kb/micro_market_desk/0.md`, finding 2.

### Verdict

**KB-RUNTIME PASS.** Every branch, object, tier, action, owner and terminal state I derived from the visible materials alone matches the source-layer solution; the whole four-problem tree was derived from the prerequisite sentences and the records with no hop pre-solved; four of the four scored parameters were reached by the source's own method, two of them to the cent and two of them one cent out on a half-cent tie whose published tie-break the source's own arithmetic does not follow. No branch of this task can be explained only by hidden compute, GT or raw `initial_state`.
